methods.conditions: Independent private arenas; real capture/fire; standard 60-unit missiles; actual complete off-screen birth checked from launch events; three defender widths; left/above/diagonal approaches; settled real camera; fixed 1650-unit distant launch or near birth 60 units beyond the ray/viewport intersection (30-unit radius plus 30-unit ray buffer; normal clearance varies with angle). 250/400ms are chosen response scenarios, not measured human reaction statistics. Perfect perpendicular direction is granted. No screenshots during a dodge.
methods.touch: Chromium trusted CDP touch input using the actual joystick. Neutral pre-held thumb, fresh acquisition and already-moving turns are separate groups. Actual event times and replicated movement are recorded; automation adds delivery overhead beyond requested waiting time.
methods.latency: A local TCP relay delays traffic by 50ms each way, including both WebSocket directions. Actual game RTT is recorded. No physical Android device was attached.
methods.outcomes: A server impact message identifies actual contact; injury/gem loss alone is not used as a proxy. All idle controls are expected to be hit. Passing an experiment means valid capture/launch/recording, not a successful dodge.
methods.limitations: Single controlled encounter per cell, open space, one incoming shot and fixed shooter classes. Not a human recognition study, population success rate, physical phone measurement, crowded-match or wall-escape certification. Near-edge origin inference can suppress the warning; those cases remain in results and are distinguished from time-budget failures.

physics.method: Actual fireCaptive, shared movement, flight, collision and KO code; baseline geometry matched; no renderer/network. 30Hz game-cadence model plus 120Hz optimistic integration. Binary search only resolves to the simulation tick. 250ms starts after observed warning lead mapped to the idle collision time; not a human recognition measurement.
